MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  OCTOBER 21, 2019

  The Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at 7:07
  p.m. at City Council Chambers 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California
  by CHAIR RETZ.

  1.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR RETZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Retz, Persichina, Romanelli, Pope, Ciarolla &
  McCormick

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Bain

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor
  Daniel A-Haja, Comm. Services Coordinator

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 16, 2019

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted one correction to the minutes to correct typographical error
  on page three.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 16, 2019 AS CORRECTED

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  TONY CAMPANELLA of 38 Harbor Sight Dr. expressed concern that not enough was
  done to notify residents of the Phase one portion of the Taber Grove project.

  Assistant City Manager Davis noted that the City uses redundant efforts to notify residents
  and for Phase Two of the project, the City plans to hold a meeting with their neighborhood
  and will communicate through the Homeowners Association and by letter sent to the
  affected radius.

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 21, 2019
   CHAIR RETZ recalled that there have been meetings and communications from the City
  about Phase One of the project. He also mentioned Andy Clark had received letters from
  Tony Campanella in regards to phase two.

  TONY CAMPANELLA stated that he and other neighbors have not received any notice on
  Phase One and that the majority of the community was not involved in the process.

  Recognizing that this item is agendized for a verbal update later on the agenda, Chair
  Retz asked COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO to provide her
  comments at this time.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

  A.  TABER GROVE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated that the cause for delay in the Phase
  one process was due to a portion of the driveway property being owned by neighbors of
  the Taber Family and that a further meeting with Willdan Engineering and the Taber family
  is scheduled for later in the week.

  CHAIR RETZ asked if the meeting would include the other family involved and if there
  would be any rerouting of the drain.

  Assistant City Manager Davis stated that staff plans to meet with the engineer to find out
  how much further involvement would be needed from the adjacent property owner.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA (CONTINUED)

  MICHAEL CHANG offered to provide a pilot program of an automated locker system that
  was operated through a smart phone application which would scan a QR code to rent out
  park recreation supplies. He explained that the locker system uses a camera that faces
  inside the door and uses smart technology to verify the proper items were returned.

  CHAIR RETZ asked what the cost would be to run the proposed pilot program within the
  City parks. CHANG responded that the cost would vary depending on door size and
  features of the locker system.

  Assistant City Manager Davis suggested staff could work with Mr. Chang in order to create
  a proposal for the City.

  CHAIR RETZ agreed and wanted to see the possible future costs of the locker system
  such as insurance.

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted that considerations should be made in regards to safety
  and finances and getting feedback from other cities who have participated would be
  appreciated.

  5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 21, 2019
   None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  VETERAN’S MEMORIAL AT CITY HALL UPDATE

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a brief overview per the agenda
  material.

  CHAIR RETZ asked if the cost of replacing the plants would be an additional cost to the
  City.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted the plants cost range from $15 to $20
  and it would be the City’s responsibility to replace them.

  Assistant City Manager Davis added the cost of plant replacement would be coordinated
  with the landscape company and would be coordinated with the City Hall’s greater
  landscape purchases and would result in no significant cost.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if there was a discussion regarding the plaque
  policy and whether the plaque meets the criteria before going forward to Council.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated that the plaque follows current policy
  in place.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA to:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATION TO RECOMMEND APPROVAL OF THE
  VETERAN’S MEMORIAL TO THE CITY COUNCIL.

  CHAIR RETZ REQUESTED A ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Ciarolla, Persichina, Retz, Pope, McCormick, Romanelli
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bain

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  None

  B.  PARADE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted that Parade Grand Marshals have been selected and
  contacted. The Parade Grand Marshal will be Paralympian Allison Compton and Sports
  Parade Grand Marshal Daryl Evans of the LA Kings. Pam Barrett-Hill and Jim Hill will be

PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 21, 2019
   Community Grand Marshals and Dale Allen will be the Hometown Marshal. The significant
  changes will be the addition of lighting and live taping of the event. Cost reduction
  was proposed through sponsorships and selling of photography packages.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  TABER GROVE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT) – TAKEN OUT OF ORDER DURING
  AUDIENCE ITEMS - SEE ABOVE

  B.  SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated that Silver Spur Little League will
  continue with the Little League Charter and that they will work with the City to work on the
  2020 draft agreement. The City Attorney has revised the agreement for 2020 which has
  been sent to the Little League. The Little League has reached out to meet with Youth
  Sports Committee, which includes Commissioners Bain, Persichina and Romanelli, to
  discuss the changes and a meeting will be scheduled shortly.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if there was any feedback on the data that backs
  their support for branching off to Pony Colt.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated that they do not plan on transitioning
  to a Pony Colt and will stay as a Little League at this time.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA suggested covering the Junior League at the meeting.

  Assistant City Manager Davis asked if the Junior League was part of the Little League
  Agreement. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA answered that they are two separate
  leagues.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTIONS OF SEPTEMBER 24, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  SPECIAL EVENT PERMITS

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted that staff is working with the City
  Attorney to streamline the permit process and to generate revenue when possible.

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  Assistant City Manager Davis noted a joint meeting on October 22 for City Celebration
  debriefing with City Council at 6:00 P.M. and Andy Clark’s Wall of Recognition Ceremony
  at 6:30P.M.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 21, 2019
   ROMANELLI to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:44 PM TO AN ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON OCTOBER 22, 2019 AT 7:00 P.M., FOR A JOINT
  MEETING WITH THE CITY COUNCIL IN THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4045
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.
